_comment: Main Task (Main Mission) cards, transcribed from the printed English cards in the Tabletop Simulator mod, cross-checked against the Korean scans on namu.wiki. The rulebook component list says the core box holds 10 Main Task Cards, and these are those 10. Card text is our English rendering of the printed Korean; the printed card always wins. Zone names (Alpha..India) are the board's tactical zones.
_confirms: Four of these (Fragment Recovery, Flank Attack, Frontal Breakthrough, Signal Reception) also appear as thumbnails in the rulebook and match our rules digest exactly.

families.name: Black Box
families.text:
Black boxes are artefacts of an ancient civilisation recovered from the ruins, and both factions want them. A black box on the board is shown with a mission marker, fills a 1x1 small grid, may overlap a unit, and blocks neither movement nor line of sight. The players place them at setup, one in each tactical zone the card names, taking turns from the First Player.

A unit picks one up when it moves through the box's position, or when its own Action Opportunity ends in the box's grid, and picking it up is optional. It needs a Part with the Freehand keyword: put the mission marker on that Part's card, and while it carries the box that Part's Freehand does not count.

When a carrying unit is Penetrated, the black box drops. The attacker places it in contact with the carrier's base, at ground level and never on top of a building.

faq.q: Can one unit hold more than one black box?
faq.a: Yes, one for each Freehand keyword it has (FAQ P7).

faq.q: Is picking up a black box compulsory?
Can the attacker choose not to make a Penetrated carrier drop its black box?
faq.a: No. The box always drops (FAQ P3).

faq.q: If a black box drops into another unit's grid, does that unit pick it up?
faq.a: No. A unit picks one up only by moving through it or by ending its own Action Opportunity in its grid, never because another unit's action ended (FAQ P8).

families.name: Occupation
families.text:
A control zone is an area that can be occupied. Normally one tactical zone is designated as one control zone, covering all the grids of that tactical area.

No marker is placed at the start. When a player takes a zone, place the mission marker with that player's colour face up; when the other player takes it, flip the marker over.

At the end of a round you occupy a control zone if you have a mech that is not in Shutdown stance, or one drone, inside the zone, and there are no enemy units in the zone. A control zone scores for its controller from the round it is occupied.

faq.q: Do projectiles and deployables count for occupying a control zone?
faq.a: Not for taking it. Only a Mech out of Shutdown Stance or a Drone can occupy a zone, and a Low Value Unit cannot, because taking a zone means interacting with a Task Item and Low Value Units may never do that (p.82).

faq.q: Can a Low Value Unit still stop the enemy taking a zone?
faq.a: No. The Supplementary Rules 1.04 give the Low Value Tag as the reason Barricades, Mines and the other Deployables cannot interact with Control Zones, and every Projectile and Low Value Drone carries that Tag, so one standing in a zone neither takes it nor stops the enemy taking it. The Excavation Claim card prints its own exclusion because its Tactical Area is not a Task Item.

faq.q: Does having more units in the zone help?
faq.a: No, the number of units does not matter.

families.name: Terminals
families.text:
A terminal is an object you access to score. Terminals are placed in a tactical area, and the area you can access them from is all the grids of that tactical area. A mission marker shows the terminal's position. It is turned face-down when the terminal is accessed, and every marker turns face-up again at the End Phase.

There are two ways in. Direct access: at the End Phase, if you have a mech that is not in Shutdown stance, or one drone, anywhere in the terminal's tactical area, and there are no enemy units there, you access it. Remote access: in these missions every mech has the Remote Access action, a Short Tactical Action performed with the Torso in its own Action Opportunity, at Range 4 of any grid of the terminal's area. It is an electronic warfare roll against the terminal, whose Electronic value is 3, and a tie goes to the mech; on success you access it.

Each terminal can only be accessed once per round.

faq.q: For direct access, does the unit have to be in the terminal's own grid?
faq.a: No. Direct access works from any grid of the tactical area the terminal sits in, and remote access may measure its Range 4 to any grid of that area (FAQ P6).

faq.q: Is remote access an Electronic Attack?
faq.a: No. It is electronic warfare, but it is neither an Electronic Attack nor Electronic Support, so the ADK60EC Raven EC Type's Repeater and the RDL's KeyHole do not affect it (FAQ P12).

families.name: VIP
families.text: A VIP mission turns one mech on each side into a Commander, named by its own player at setup. Destroying the enemy's Commander scores, and the game then ends at that round's End Phase.

cards.name: Black Box: Fragment Recovery
cards.setup: Place 1 black box in each of the Bravo, Charlie, Delta, Echo, Golf, Foxtrot and Hotel tactical zones.
cards.scoring: At the end of Round 5, each player scores 2 VP for every black box they hold.
cards.deployment: Black 3x5 and White 3x5, in opposite corners

cards.name: Black Box: Key Facility
cards.setup: Place 1 black box in each of the Bravo, Delta, Echo, Foxtrot and Hotel tactical zones.
cards.scoring: At the end of Round 5, each player scores 4 VP for every black box they hold.
cards.deployment: Black 2x12 and White 2x12, along opposite edges

cards.name: Black Box: Asset Preservation
cards.setup: Place 1 black box in each of the Alpha, Charlie, Golf and India tactical zones.
cards.scoring: At the end of Round 5, each player scores 4 VP for every black box they hold that is in the Echo zone. Boxes have to be carried to the centre to count.
cards.deployment: Black 2x12 and White 2x12, along opposite edges

cards.name: Occupation: Outflank
cards.setup: The Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Golf, Hotel and India tactical zones become control zones. All start uncontrolled.
cards.scoring: From Round 2 onward, score 1 VP for each control zone you hold.
cards.deployment: Black 3x5 and White 3x5, in opposite corners

cards.name: Occupation: Forward Advance
cards.setup: The Bravo, Echo and Hotel tactical zones become control zones. All start uncontrolled.
cards.scoring: From Round 2 onward, score 2 VP for each control zone you hold.
cards.deployment: Black 3x5 and White 3x5, in opposite corners

cards.name: Occupation: Long and Deep
cards.setup: The Alpha, Echo and India tactical zones become control zones. All start uncontrolled. Alpha and India sit in the two deployment corners, so each side begins next to one of them.
cards.scoring: From Round 2 onward, score 2 VP for each control zone you hold.
cards.deployment: Black 3x5 and White 3x5, in opposite corners

cards.name: Terminals: Data Theft
cards.setup: Place 1 terminal in each of the Bravo, Charlie, Golf and Hotel tactical zones.
cards.scoring: Score 2 VP for each terminal you access.
cards.deployment: Black 3x5 and White 3x5, in opposite corners

cards.name: Terminals: Receive Signal
cards.setup: Place 1 terminal in each of the Bravo, Echo and Hotel tactical zones.
cards.scoring: Score 2 VP for each terminal you access.
cards.deployment: Black 2x12 and White 2x12, along opposite edges

cards.name: Terminals: Geological Exploration
cards.setup: Place 1 terminal in each of the Bravo, Delta, Foxtrot and Hotel tactical zones.
cards.scoring: Score 2 VP for each terminal you access.
cards.deployment: Black 3x5 and White 3x5, in opposite corners

cards.name: VIP: Assassination
cards.setup: In the mission preparation step each player designates one of their own mechs as the Commander.
cards.scoring: When one player's Commander is Destroyed, the other player gains 10 Victory Points and the game ends. If neither Commander is destroyed after 5 rounds, each player gains 3 Victory Points for each Part of the Enemy Commander that has been Destroyed.
cards.deployment: Black 2x12 and White 2x12, along opposite edges
